plan: 2 Samuel 5:1-3; 1 Chronicles 11:1-3; 1 Chronicles 12:23-40; 2 Samuel 5:17-25; 1 Chronicles 14:8-17; 2 Samuel 5:6-10; 1 Chronicles 11:4-9; 1 Chronicles 3:4b; 2 Samuel 5:13, 4-5, 11-12; 1 Chronicles 14:1-2; 1 Chronicles 13:1-5; 2 Samuel 6:1-11; 1 Chronicles 13:6-14

readings.title: Dawiḏ Crowned Over All Yisra’ĕl
readings.subtitle: The Elders Come to Ḥeḇron
readings.text: [2 Samuel 5:1] And all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl came to Dawiḏ at Ḥeḇron and spoke, saying, “See, we are your bone and your flesh. [2] And in times past, when Sha’ul was sovereign over us, you were the one who led <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl out and brought them in. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to you, <dq>‘You shepherd <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl, and be ruler over Yisra’ĕl.’</dq> ” [3] So all the elders of Yisra’ĕl came to the sovereign at Ḥeḇron, and Sovereign Dawiḏ made a covenant with them at Ḥeḇron before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And they anointed <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ sovereign over Yisra’ĕl. [1 Chronicles 11:1] And all Yisra’ĕl gathered to Dawiḏ at Ḥeḇron, saying, “See, we are your bone and your flesh. [2] Even in times past, even when Sha’ul was sovereign, you were the one who led <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl out and brought them in. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> said to you, <dq>‘You shepherd <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl, and be ruler over <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl.’</dq> ” [3] So all the elders of Yisra’ĕl came to the sovereign at Ḥeḇron, and Dawiḏ made a covenant with them at Ḥeḇron before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And they anointed <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ sovereign over Yisra’ĕl, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> by the hand of Shemu’ĕl.

readings.title: The Armies That Came to Dawiḏ
readings.subtitle: Mighty Men of Yisra’ĕl Gather
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 12:23] And these are the numbers of the divisions equipped for army duty, who came to Dawiḏ at Ḥeḇron, to turn over <dn>את</dn> the reign of Sha’ul to him, according to the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>: [24] of the children of Yehuḏah, bearing shield and spear, six thousand eight hundred, equipped for army duty; [25] of the children of Shim‛on, mighty brave men for the army, seven thousand one hundred; [26] of the children of Lĕwi, four thousand six hundred; [27] and Yehoyaḏa, the leader of the Aharonites, and with him three thousand seven hundred; [28] and Tsaḏoq, a young man, a mighty brave one, and from his father’s house twenty-two heads; [29] and of the children of Binyamin, relatives of Sha’ul, three thousand – until then the greatest part of them had kept their allegiance to the house of Sha’ul; [30] and of the children of Ephrayim twenty-eight thousand eight hundred, mighty brave men, men of name in their father’s house; [31] and of the half-tribe of Menashsheh eighteen thousand, who were designated by name to come and make <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ sovereign; [32] and of the children of Yissasḵar who had understanding of the times, to know what Yisra’ĕl should do, their heads were two hundred. And all their brothers were at their command; [33] of Zeḇulun fifty thousand who went out to battle, expert in war with all weapons of war, to help with an undivided heart; [34] and of Naphtali one thousand combat leaders, and with them thirty-seven thousand with shield and spear; [35] and of the Danites who could draw up in battle formation, twenty-eight thousand six hundred; [36] and of Ashĕr, those who go out to battle, expert in war, forty thousand; [37] and from beyond the Yardĕn, of the Re’uḇĕnites and the Gaḏites and the half-tribe of Menashsheh, one hundred and twenty thousand, with all kinds of weapons of battle for war. [38] All these men of battle, who could draw up in battle formation, came to Ḥeḇron with a perfect heart, to make <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ sovereign over all Yisra’ĕl. And all the rest of Yisra’ĕl were of one heart to make <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ sovereign. [39] And they were there with Dawiḏ three days, eating and drinking, for their brothers had prepared for them. [40] And also those who were near to them, from as far away as Yissasḵar and Zeḇulun and Naphtali, were bringing food on donkeys and camels, on mules and oxen – food of flour and cakes of figs and cakes of raisins, and wine and oil and cattle and sheep, in abundance, for there was rejoicing in Yisra’ĕl.

readings.title: Defeating the Pelishtim
readings.subtitle: The Breakthrough of Water
readings.text: [2 Samuel 5:17] And the Pelishtim heard that they had anointed <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ sovereign over Yisra’ĕl, and all the Pelishtim went up to search for <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ. And Dawiḏ heard of it and went down to the stronghold. [18] And the Pelishtim had come and spread out in the Valley of Repha’im. [19] And Dawiḏ inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “Do I go up against the Pelishtim? Do <dn>You</dn> give them into my hand?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Dawiḏ, <dq>“Go up, for <dn>I</dn> shall certainly give the Pelishtim into your hand.”</dq> [20] And Dawiḏ came to Ba‛al Peratsim, and Dawiḏ smote them there, and said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has broken through <dn>את</dn> my enemies before me, like a breakthrough of water.” Therefore he called the name of that place Ba‛al Peratsim. [21] And they left their idols there, and Dawiḏ and his men took them away. [22] And the Pelishtim came up once again and spread out in the Valley of Repha’im. [23] And Dawiḏ inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Do not go up. Turn around behind them, and come upon them in front of the mulberry trees.</dq> [24] <dq>And it shall be, when you hear <dn>את</dn> the sound of stepping in the tops of the mulberry trees, then act promptly, for then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall go out before you to smite the camp of the Pelishtim.”</dq> [25] And Dawiḏ did so, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded him, and smote <dn>את</dn> the Pelishtim from Geḇa as far as Gezer. [1 Chronicles 14:8] And the Pelishtim heard that Dawiḏ had been anointed sovereign over all Yisra’ĕl, and all the Pelishtim went up to search for <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ. And Dawiḏ heard of it and went out against them. [9] And the Pelishtim had come and made a raid in the Valley of Repha’im. [10] And Dawiḏ inquired of <dn>Elohim</dn>, saying, “Do I go up against the Pelishtim? And shall <dn>You</dn> give them into my hand?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Go up, and <dn>I</dn> shall give them into your hand.”</dq> [11] And they went up to Ba‛al Peratsim, and Dawiḏ smote them there. And Dawiḏ said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has broken through <dn>את</dn> my enemies by my hand like a breakthrough of water.” Therefore they called the name of that place Ba‛al Peratsim. [12] And they left their mighty ones there, and Dawiḏ gave the command, and they were burned with fire. [13] And the Pelishtim made another raid in the valley. [14] And Dawiḏ inquired again of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>Elohim</dn> said to him, <dq>“Do not go up after them. Turn away from them, and come upon them in front of the mulberry trees.</dq> [15] <dq>And it shall be, when you hear <dn>את</dn> a sound of stepping in the tops of the mulberry trees, then go out to battle, for <dn>Elohim</dn> has gone out before you to smite the camp of the Pelishtim.”</dq> [16] And Dawiḏ did as <dn>Elohim</dn> commanded him, and they smote <dn>את</dn> the camp of the Pelishtim from Giḇ‛on as far as Gezer. [17] And the name of Dawiḏ went out into all lands, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> put the fear of him upon all nations.

readings.title: The Capture of Yerushalayim
readings.subtitle: The Stronghold of Tsiyon
readings.text: [2 Samuel 5:6] And the sovereign and his men went to Yerushalayim against the Yeḇusites, the inhabitants of the land, who spoke to Dawiḏ, saying, “You do not come in here, unless you take away the blind and the lame,” saying, “Dawiḏ does not come in here.” [7] But Dawiḏ captured <dn>את</dn> the stronghold of Tsiyon, which is the City of Dawiḏ. [8] And Dawiḏ said on that day, “Anyone smiting the Yeḇusites, let him go by the water shaft and smite the lame and the blind, who are hated by Dawiḏ’s being.” Therefore they say, “The blind and the lame do not come into the house.” [9] And Dawiḏ dwelt in the stronghold, and called it the City of Dawiḏ. And Dawiḏ built all around from the Millo and inward. [10] And Dawiḏ went on and became great, and <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of hosts was with him. [1 Chronicles 11:4] And Dawiḏ and all Yisra’ĕl went to Yerushalayim, which is Yeḇus, where the Yeḇusites were, the inhabitants of the land. [5] And the inhabitants of Yeḇus said to Dawiḏ, “You do not come in here.” But Dawiḏ captured <dn>את</dn> the stronghold of Tsiyon, which is the City of Dawiḏ. [6] And Dawiḏ said, “Anyone smiting the Yeḇusites first becomes chief and commander.” And Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah went up first, and became chief. [7] And Dawiḏ dwelt in the stronghold, therefore they called it the City of Dawiḏ. [8] And he built <dn>את</dn> the city around it, from the Millo to the surrounding area, and Yo’aḇ restored <dn>את</dn> the rest of the city. [9] And Dawiḏ went on and became great, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts was with him.

readings.title: Dawiḏ’s Establishment
readings.subtitle: Building a House and a Kingdom
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 3:4] And he reigned in Yerushalayim thirty-three years. [2 Samuel 5:13] And Dawiḏ took more concubines and wives from Yerushalayim, after he had come from Ḥeḇron. And more sons and daughters were born to Dawiḏ. [4] Dawiḏ was thirty years old when he began to reign; he reigned forty years. [5] In Ḥeḇron he reigned over Yehuḏah seven years and six months, and in Yerushalayim he reigned thirty-three years over all Yisra’ĕl and Yehuḏah. [11] And Ḥiram sovereign of Tsor sent messengers to Dawiḏ, and cedar trees, and carpenters and masons. And they built Dawiḏ a house. [12] And Dawiḏ knew that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had established him as sovereign over Yisra’ĕl, and that <dn>He</dn> had exalted <dn>His</dn> reign for the sake of <dn>His</dn> people Yisra’ĕl. [1 Chronicles 14:1] And Ḥiram sovereign of Tsor sent messengers to Dawiḏ, and cedar trees, and masons and carpenters, to build him a house. [2] And Dawiḏ knew that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had established him as sovereign over Yisra’ĕl, for his reign was highly exalted for the sake of <dn>His</dn> people Yisra’ĕl.

readings.title: Moving the Ark of Elohim
readings.subtitle: The Threshing-Floor of Naḵon
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 13:1] And Dawiḏ consulted with the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and with every leader. [2] And Dawiḏ said to all the assembly of Yisra’ĕl, “If it seems good to you, and if it is of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, let us send out to our brothers everywhere who are left in all the land of Yisra’ĕl, as well as to the priests and Lĕwites who are in their cities and their open lands, to gather together to us, [3] and let us bring the ark of our <dn>Elohim</dn> back to us, for we have not inquired at it since the days of Sha’ul.” [4] And all the assembly agreed to do so, for the word was right in the eyes of all the people. [5] So Dawiḏ gathered <dn>את</dn> all Yisra’ĕl together, from Shiḥor in Mitsrayim to as far as the entrance of Ḥamath, to bring <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> from Qiryath Ye‛arim. [2 Samuel 6:1] And Dawiḏ again gathered <dn>את</dn> all the chosen men of Yisra’ĕl, thirty thousand. [2] And Dawiḏ arose and went with all the people who were with him from Ba‛alĕy Yehuḏah, to bring up from there <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>, whose name is called by the Name, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, who dwells between the keruḇim. [3] And they placed <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> on a new wagon, and brought it out of the house of Aḇinaḏaḇ, which was on the hill. And Uzzah and Aḥyo, the sons of Aḇinaḏaḇ, were leading <dn>את</dn> the new wagon. [4] And they brought it out of the house of Aḇinaḏaḇ, which was on the hill, accompanying the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and Aḥyo went before the ark. [5] And Dawiḏ and all the house of Yisra’ĕl played music before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on all kinds of instruments of fir wood, on lyres, on harps, on tambourines, on sistrums, and on cymbals. [6] And when they came to the threshing-floor of Naḵon, Uzzah reached out toward the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled. [7] And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Uzzah, and <dn>Elohim</dn> smote him there for the fault. And he died there by the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>. [8] And Dawiḏ was displeased because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had broken out against Uzzah. And he called the name of the place Perets Uzzah, to this day. [9] And Dawiḏ was afraid of <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> that day, and said, “How does the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> come to me?” [10] And Dawiḏ would not move <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> with him into the City of Dawiḏ, but Dawiḏ took it aside into the house of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom the Gittite. [11] And the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> remained in the house of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom the Gittite three months. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> blessed <dn>את</dn> Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom and <dn>את</dn> all his house. [1 Chronicles 13:6] And Dawiḏ and all Yisra’ĕl went up to Ba‛alah, to Qiryath Ye‛arim, which belonged to Yehuḏah, to bring up from there <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim YeHoVaH</dn>, who dwells between the keruḇim, where <dn>His</dn> Name is called on. [7] And they placed <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> on a new wagon from the house of Aḇinaḏaḇ, and Uzza and Aḥyo were leading the wagon. [8] And Dawiḏ and all Yisra’ĕl played music before <dn>Elohim</dn> with all their might, with songs and with lyres, and with harps, and with tambourines, and with cymbals, and with trumpets. [9] And when they came to the threshing-floor of Kiḏon, Uzza reached out his hand to hold <dn>את</dn> the ark, for the oxen stumbled. [10] And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Uzza, and <dn>He</dn> smote him because he put his hand to the ark. And he died there before <dn>Elohim</dn>. [11] And Dawiḏ was displeased because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had broken out against Uzza. Therefore that place is called Perets Uzza, to this day. [12] And Dawiḏ was afraid of <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> that day, saying, “How do I bring <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> to me?” [13] And Dawiḏ did not take <dn>את</dn> the ark with him into the City of Dawiḏ, but took it aside into the house of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom the Gittite. [14] And the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> remained with the household of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom in his house three months. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> blessed <dn>את</dn> the house of Oḇĕḏ-Eḏom and all that he had.
